angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-01.question: What is the current minimum catch size (Mindestmass) for pike (Esox lucius) in North Rhine-Westphalia?

options.a: 30 cm
options.b: 35 cm
options.c: 45 cm
options.d: 60 cm

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-01.explanation: Pike in NRW have a minimum size of 45 cm, and additionally a closed season from 15 February to 30 April during which pike may not be taken at all. Closed seasons and minimum sizes are set by the Landesfischereiverordnung under the authority granted by §42(1)(a) and (b) LFischG NRW.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-02.question: During which period does the closed season for zander (pikeperch) apply in NRW?

options.a: 1 January to 28 February
options.b: 1 April to 31 May
options.c: 1 July to 31 August
options.d: 1 October to 30 November

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-02.explanation: Zander are protected in NRW from 1 April to 31 May, matching their spring spawning period. The minimum size for zander is 40 cm.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-03.question: What is the minimum size for eel in North Rhine-Westphalia?

options.a: 50 cm
options.b: 35 cm
options.c: 25 cm
options.d: No minimum size, since it is protected year-round

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-03.explanation: Eel in NRW have a minimum size of 50 cm statewide, plus a closed season in the Rhine main channel (excluding tributaries) from 1 October to 1 March, aimed in particular at protecting silver eels (Blankaale) as they migrate out to spawn.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-04.question: Which fish species is protected year-round in NRW and generally may not be taken at all?

options.a: Salmon (Salmo salar)
options.b: Carp
options.c: Tench
options.d: Ide (Aland)

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-04.explanation: Salmon enjoy year-round protection in NRW, since native salmon populations have only been rebuilt through costly reintroduction programmes and remain highly vulnerable to fishing pressure. A minimum size is therefore irrelevant for salmon - it may not be taken at all.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-05.question: What is the minimum size for brown trout in NRW?

options.a: 15 cm
options.b: 20 cm
options.c: 25 cm
options.d: 40 cm

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-05.explanation: Brown trout in NRW have a minimum size of 25 cm. Their closed season runs from 20 October to 15 March, covering their winter spawning period, which is typical for salmonids.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-06.question: When is barbel protected by a closed season in North Rhine-Westphalia?

options.a: 1 January to 28 February
options.b: 15 May to 15 June
options.c: 1 September to 31 October
options.d: It has no closed season

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-06.explanation: Barbel are protected from 15 May to 15 June, when they spawn on gravel beds in fast-flowing rivers. Their minimum size in NRW is 35 cm.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-07.question: Which fish has a 30 cm minimum size and a closed season from 1 March to 30 April in NRW?

options.a: Grayling
options.b: Carp
options.c: Tench
options.d: Wels catfish

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-07.explanation: Grayling have a 30 cm minimum size in NRW and are protected from 1 March to 30 April. Nase (a rheophilic cyprinid) share the same closed period, since both species spawn in spring.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-08.question: What must be done with a fish caught alive that is below the prescribed minimum size?

options.a: It may still be killed and eaten at home
options.b: It must be released gently and immediately, ideally without removing it from the water
options.c: It may be kept in a keep net and released later
options.d: It must be measured and can then be dealt with at the angler's discretion

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-08.explanation: Undersized fish must be released gently and immediately - ideally without even lifting them out of the water, handled with wet hands and carefully unhooked. §42(1)(b) and (c) LFischG NRW authorizes the Landesfischereiverordnung to regulate minimum sizes and the treatment of undersized fish or fish caught during a closed season.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-09.question: Which of the following fish species has NO closed season in NRW (but does have a 35 cm minimum size)?

options.a: Pike
options.b: Zander
options.c: Carp
options.d: Grayling

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-09.explanation: Carp have a 35 cm minimum size in NRW but no statutory closed season, since stocked carp in ponds and still waters are largely artificially propagated and the species is not treated as needing the same protection as wild-reproducing river species.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-10.question: What is the minimum size for lake trout (Seeforelle) in North Rhine-Westphalia?

options.a: 25 cm
options.b: 50 cm
options.c: 70 cm
options.d: No minimum size

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-10.explanation: Lake trout have one of the highest minimum sizes among NRW fish species at 50 cm, sharing the same closed season (20 October to 15 March) as the closely related brown trout.

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-11.question: What is a 'Laichschonbezirk' (spawning sanctuary) under §44 LFischG NRW?

options.a: A stretch of water where only club members may fish
options.b: A section of water designated by regulation of the upper fisheries authority as being an especially suitable spawning/nursery area and given time-limited or permanent protection
options.c: A body of water reserved exclusively for commercial fishing
options.d: A private fishing water with no official oversight

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-11.explanation: Under §44(1)(b) LFischG NRW, the upper fisheries authority, in agreement with the upper water authority, may by regulation designate sections of water that are especially suitable spawning/nursery grounds as spawning sanctuaries; fishing and disruptive activities there can be restricted or banned for set periods (§44(2)).

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-12.question: What does §43 LFischG NRW require regarding permanent fishing installations (e.g. traps) during a closed season?

options.a: They must be removed or taken out of operation for the duration of the closed season, unless the fisheries authority allows an exception
options.b: They may keep operating unchanged as long as protected species are released
options.c: They must be checked daily during the closed season but need not be dismantled
options.d: They are not specially regulated during closed seasons

angelschein-nrw-schonzeiten-12.explanation: §43 LFischG NRW requires permanent fishing installations to be removed or shut down for the duration of closed seasons; the fisheries authority may grant exceptions if this does not endanger the fish stock or its stewardship.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-01.question: Which of the following methods is generally prohibited when fishing in NRW under §39(1) LFischG?

options.a: Fly fishing
options.b: Using artificial light, or explosive, stupefying or poisonous substances
options.c: Fishing with a wobbler lure
options.d: Fishing with live baitfish

angelschein-nrw-geraete-01.explanation: §39(1) LFischG NRW bans the use of artificial light and explosive, stupefying or poisonous substances, as well as any injuring device other than the ordinary fish hook, when fishing. Violating this is among the most serious breaches of fisheries law.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-02.question: Can any angler in NRW fish using electricity (electrofishing)?

options.a: Yes, as long as they hold a Fischereischein
options.b: Yes, without any restriction
options.c: No, electrofishing is only permitted under the conditions set by regulation under §39(3) LFischG, and generally requires special authorization
options.d: No, it is banned without exception

angelschein-nrw-geraete-02.explanation: Electrofishing is a heavily regulated special method, usually reserved for people holding an operator's certificate plus official authorization, e.g. for stock surveys. §39(3) LFischG empowers the Ministry to set, by regulation, the conditions under which fishing using electric current is permitted; without meeting those conditions it is prohibited.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-03.question: What is the minimum required length of the steel leader (Stahlvorfach) when pike fishing with dead baitfish?

options.a: At least 40 cm
options.b: At least 10 cm
options.c: A steel leader is not required by law
options.d: At least 100 cm

angelschein-nrw-geraete-03.explanation: When pike fishing with dead baitfish, the steel leader should be at least 40 cm long, so the pike cannot bite through the line and swim off with a deeply swallowed hook, which would cause it severe suffering. With artificial lures, a minimum of about 20 cm is generally sufficient.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-04.question: May an angler carry ready-to-fish tackle at a body of water where they have no right to fish?

options.a: Yes, as long as they do not actually cast it
options.b: Yes, if accompanied by an authorized person
options.c: No - §49 LFischG NRW prohibits carrying fishing tackle in ready-to-use condition at or on waters where no fishing right exists
options.d: Yes, provided the tackle is limited to fewer than two rods

angelschein-nrw-geraete-04.explanation: §49 LFischG NRW states: no one may carry fishing tackle in ready-to-use condition at or on waters where they have no right to fish. Assembled, rigged tackle already creates the appearance of an intent to fish unlawfully; packed-away, unusable tackle is not covered.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-05.question: May live baitfish be used without restriction when angling in NRW?

options.a: Yes, on all waters with no further conditions
options.b: No, their use is only permitted if the water/club regulations expressly allow it
options.c: No, live baitfish are completely banned throughout NRW
options.d: Yes, provided the baitfish comes from a different federal state

angelschein-nrw-geraete-05.explanation: Using live baitfish is subject to particular animal-welfare scrutiny. In practice it is only permitted where the relevant water or club regulations expressly allow it; many NRW water regulations exclude it entirely on animal-welfare grounds.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-06.question: What is a 'Rachensperre' (jaw spreader/gag)?

options.a: A fish disease affecting the throat
options.b: A prohibited piece of fishing tackle
options.c: A tool used when landing and unhooking predatory fish like pike and zander that holds the jaws open, preventing bites and reducing injury to both angler and fish
options.d: A device used to stun the fish before killing it

angelschein-nrw-geraete-06.explanation: The jaw spreader (Rachensperre) is a permitted aid used when landing predatory fish (especially pike and zander) to keep the jaws open so the hook can be removed quickly and safely without injuring the angler or the fish - it serves proper, humane handling, not the catching itself.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-07.question: What equipment must an angler in NRW always carry so a caught, legal-size fish can be handled humanely?

options.a: Only a spare fishing rod
options.b: A landing net, a tape measure, a priest/priest club, a knife, and a hook disgorger
options.c: Only a keep net
options.d: Binoculars for birdwatching

angelschein-nrw-geraete-07.explanation: So that a caught fish above the minimum size can be stunned and killed immediately without unnecessary suffering, every angler's basic kit must include: a landing net (for a gentle landing), a tape measure (to check the minimum size), a priest/club for stunning, a knife for the fatal heart cut, and a hook disgorger.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-08.question: Are fish hooks among the 'injuring devices' banned under §39(1) LFischG NRW?

options.a: Yes, every hook needs an official exemption
options.b: No, the fish hook is expressly excluded from that ban
options.c: Yes, only single hooks are allowed, treble hooks are banned
options.d: No, but only in fly fishing

angelschein-nrw-geraete-08.explanation: §39(1) LFischG NRW bans 'injuring devices' in general, but expressly exempts the ordinary fish hook - it is the core, statutorily recognized tool of angling.

angelschein-nrw-geraete-09.question: In NRW, which legal provision regulates how many hand rods an angler may fish with at the same time?

options.a: The state fisheries law (LFischG NRW)
options.b: The state fisheries ordinance (LFischVO NRW)
options.c: This is not regulated by law - the number is set solely by the water/permit regulations of the relevant permit issuer
options.d: Every angler may set out an unlimited number of rods at once

angelschein-nrw-geraete-09.explanation: The number of permitted hand rods in NRW is not regulated by law - neither by the Landesfischereigesetz nor by the Landesfischereiverordnung. It is set exclusively by the water regulations (Gewaesserordnung) or permit conditions of the respective fishing-rights holder. This matches the official answer in the NRW fisheries exam question catalogue (Gesetzeskunde, question 36: 'not regulated by law').

angelschein-nrw-geraete-10.question: Why must set rods (e.g. bottom fishing or overnight carp fishing) be constantly supervised?

options.a: So a hooked fish is not left fighting the line for hours in unnecessary stress and suffering, and can be landed and dealt with promptly
options.b: Only so the tackle is not stolen
options.c: Only so waterbirds do not eat the bait
options.d: There is no legal duty of supervision at all; it is a pure recommendation with no animal-welfare basis

angelschein-nrw-geraete-10.explanation: Unsupervised rods can leave a hooked fish struggling against the line for hours or overnight, causing significant, avoidable suffering that conflicts with the principle in §1 TierSchG (no causing pain without reasonable cause). Constant supervision of set rods is therefore an integral part of ethical, humane angling (Waidgerechtigkeit) in NRW.

angelschein-nrw-recht-01.question: What is generally required to obtain a Fischereischein (fishing licence) in NRW?

options.a: Membership in an angling club
options.b: Successfully passing the Fischerpruefung (fishing exam), unless a statutory exception applies
options.c: A minimum age of 21
options.d: Proof of owning one's own body of water

angelschein-nrw-recht-01.explanation: Under §31(3) LFischG NRW, the Fischereischein may generally only be issued to people who have successfully passed the Fischerpruefung. Exceptions exist for, among others, professionally trained fishers, scientifically trained staff, and holders of a Jugendfischereischein.

angelschein-nrw-recht-02.question: From what age can a regular Fischereischein (not just the youth licence) be issued in NRW if the exam has been passed?

options.a: From age 10
options.b: From age 12
options.c: From age 14
options.d: From age 18

angelschein-nrw-recht-02.explanation: Under §32(1) LFischG NRW, people who have turned 10 but not yet 16 may only be issued a Jugendfischereischein (youth licence) - unless they have passed the Fischerpruefung AND turned 14. So a regular Fischereischein only becomes possible from age 14, and only with a passed exam.

angelschein-nrw-recht-03.question: What restriction applies to the holder of a Jugendfischereischein (youth fishing licence) in NRW?

options.a: They may only fish while accompanied by a holder of a regular Fischereischein
options.b: They may only fish on weekends
options.c: They may only catch coarse fish, never predatory species
options.d: They may only use a single hand rod

angelschein-nrw-recht-03.explanation: §32(2) LFischG NRW provides that the youth licence only authorizes fishing while accompanied by a holder of a regular Fischereischein (the fisheries authority may allow exceptions for people training as professional fishers). A youth licence can be issued to people from age 10 (§32(1)) who have not yet passed the Fischerpruefung.

angelschein-nrw-recht-04.question: Can a regular Fischereischein be issued in NRW to someone who has not yet turned 14?

options.a: Yes, without any restriction
options.b: Yes, if a parent/guardian consents in writing
options.c: No - under §33(1) No. 1 LFischG, the licence must be refused to anyone who has not yet turned 14 (at most, the youth licence from age 10 is available)
options.d: Yes, if the Fischerpruefung has already been passed

angelschein-nrw-recht-04.explanation: §33(1) No. 1 LFischG NRW lists as a mandatory ground for refusal that the Fischereischein must be denied to persons who have not yet turned 14. Younger people (from age 10) can only obtain the supervision-required Jugendfischereischein under §32.

angelschein-nrw-recht-05.question: Can the Fischereischein be refused due to past violations?

options.a: No, prior convictions are irrelevant to the fishing licence
options.b: Yes - it may be refused, among other reasons, to people who within the last three years were convicted of violating fisheries law or of animal cruelty
options.c: Yes, but only for road traffic convictions
options.d: No, except for poaching convictions committed abroad

angelschein-nrw-recht-05.explanation: §33(2) LFischG NRW lists discretionary grounds for refusal including final convictions for poaching, forging a fishing licence, or violating fisheries regulations or animal cruelty within the last three years (§33(2) Nos. 1-3). If a clean certificate of good conduct is presented, the ground for refusal no longer applies (§33(3)).

angelschein-nrw-recht-06.question: For what periods can a regular Fischereischein be issued in NRW?

options.a: Only for a single year, after which the exam must be retaken
options.b: Only indefinitely, for life
options.c: As an annual licence or for five consecutive calendar years
options.d: Only for the duration of one calendar month

angelschein-nrw-recht-06.explanation: §34(1) LFischG NRW provides two options: the Fischereischein is issued either as a one-year licence (for one calendar year) or for five consecutive calendar years, using a form set by the Ministry. Retaking the Fischerpruefung is not required to renew it.

angelschein-nrw-recht-07.question: Which authority in NRW is responsible for issuing the Fischereischein?

options.a: The relevant angling club
options.b: The municipality (Gemeinde)
options.c: The Fischereiverband NRW (state angling association)
options.d: The Bezirksregierung (district government)

angelschein-nrw-recht-07.explanation: Under §35 LFischG NRW, the municipality is responsible for issuing the Fischereischein - in practice usually the local regulatory office (Ordnungsamt) of the applicant's home municipality. The state angling association and clubs organize the Fischerpruefung itself, but not the issuance of the licence.

angelschein-nrw-recht-08.question: What is the purpose of the Fischereiabgabe (fisheries levy) collected alongside the Fischereischein fee?

options.a: General funding of the state budget
options.b: It goes to the supreme fisheries authority and, after consulting the fisheries advisory board, is used to promote fisheries
options.c: It is paid out as a bonus to fisheries wardens
options.d: It funds municipal road construction projects

angelschein-nrw-recht-08.explanation: §36(2) LFischG NRW provides that a fisheries levy equal in amount to the Fischereischein fee is collected, flows to the supreme fisheries authority and, after consulting the fisheries advisory board, must be used to promote fisheries - e.g. water stewardship, stocking measures, or research.

angelschein-nrw-recht-09.question: When does an angler in NRW additionally need a Fischereierlaubnisschein (fishing permit) on top of the Fischereischein?

options.a: Whenever they fish a water where they are neither the fishing-rights holder nor the leaseholder
options.b: Only when engaging in electrofishing
options.c: Only if they are under 18
options.d: A permit is generally no longer required in NRW

angelschein-nrw-recht-09.explanation: §37(1) LFischG NRW requires that anyone fishing a water where they are neither the fishing-rights holder nor the leaseholder must, independently of the Fischereischein (§31), carry a permit and hand it over on request. The Fischereischein alone therefore does not authorize fishing in any water of one's choosing.

angelschein-nrw-recht-10.question: What does the 'right of bank access' (Uferbetretungsrecht) for authorized anglers under §20 LFischG NRW cover?

options.a: The right to enter, at one's own risk, adjoining banks, islands and water structures for the purpose of fishing, as long as no public-law rules prevent it
options.b: An unrestricted right to enter any property including dwellings along the bank
options.c: The right to remove fences in order to reach the water
options.d: A right that applies only to commercial fishers, not anglers

angelschein-nrw-recht-10.explanation: §20(1) LFischG NRW grants authorized anglers and their helpers the right to enter, at their own risk, adjoining banks, islands, landing points, and structures such as bridges, weirs and locks for the purpose of fishing, as long as no public-law rules prevent it. This right expressly does not extend to buildings or the immediate house/residential/yard area (§20(4)).

angelschein-nrw-recht-11.question: Are competitive angling contests (judged purely on catch results) permitted in NRW?

options.a: Yes, if at least ten clubs take part
options.b: No - §50(2) LFischG NRW expressly bans this kind of competition fishing (Wettfischen)
options.c: Yes, without restriction, as long as the fisheries authority approves it
options.d: Yes, but only for children and teenagers

angelschein-nrw-recht-11.explanation: §50(2) LFischG NRW expressly bans 'Wettfischen' - a fishing event whose sole or main purpose is to rank multiple participants by their catch results. This conflicts with the principle of Waidgerechtigkeit (ethical angling), under which fish must not be reduced to a mere object of competition.

angelschein-nrw-recht-12.question: What is the purpose of the Sonderfischereischein (special licence) under §32a LFischG NRW?

options.a: It is a short-term permit for tourists who have not passed the exam
options.b: It is issued only to commercial fishers
options.c: It can be issued to people who cannot take the Fischerpruefung due to a physical, mental or psychological disability, and authorizes fishing while accompanied by a Fischereischein holder
options.d: It has fully replaced the regular Fischereischein in NRW since 2020

angelschein-nrw-recht-12.explanation: §32a LFischG NRW allows a special licence to be issued to people who cannot take the Fischerpruefung due to a physical, mental or psychological disability. Like the youth licence, it only authorizes fishing while accompanied by a holder of a regular Fischereischein, and is issued for one calendar year or for five years.

angelschein-nrw-recht-13.question: What knowledge must be demonstrated in the Fischerpruefung under §31(6) LFischG NRW?

options.a: Adequate knowledge of fish, of fishing tackle and its use, of handling caught fish, and of fisheries and animal-welfare law
options.b: Only practical casting technique with a fishing rod
options.c: Only the names of native fish species
options.d: Knowledge of commercial fishery business management

angelschein-nrw-recht-13.explanation: §31(6) LFischG NRW specifies that the Fischerpruefung must demonstrate adequate knowledge of fish, of fishing tackle and its use, of handling caught fish, and of fisheries and animal-welfare regulations - matching the official catalog's exam areas of fish biology, limnology, nature/animal protection, tackle knowledge and legal knowledge.

angelschein-nrw-recht-14.question: Is a Fischereischein obtained in another German federal state also valid in NRW?

options.a: No, a separate exam must always be taken in NRW
options.b: Yes - a licence issued in another federal state is also valid in NRW, provided the holder has or had their permanent residence there
options.c: Only if NRW additionally requires a supplementary exam
options.d: Only for tourists from abroad, not for German nationals

angelschein-nrw-recht-14.explanation: §31(7) LFischG NRW recognizes a licence issued in another federal state as valid in NRW too, provided the holder has, or had at the time of issue, their permanent residence there. In addition, §31(4) recognizes exams passed elsewhere if the candidate's residence at the time of the exam was not in NRW.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-01.question: What organ do fish primarily use to take up oxygen from the water?

options.a: The swim bladder
options.b: The gills
options.c: The lateral line
options.d: The mucous coat alone

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-01.explanation: Fish absorb dissolved oxygen through their gills: water flows over the heavily vascularized gill filaments, where gas exchange occurs. Under oxygen shortage, fish often flare their gill covers to increase the respiratory surface.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-02.question: What is the function of a fish's lateral line?

options.a: It is a sensory organ for detecting water pressure waves and currents
options.b: It is used for reproduction
options.c: It exists purely for the fish's coloration
options.d: It has no known function

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-02.explanation: The lateral line is a sensory organ running along a fish's flanks that detects tiny pressure changes and water currents. This lets fish sense prey, obstacles and other fish even in poor visibility.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-03.question: What does 'Rogner' mean in German angling terminology?

options.a: A specific fish species
options.b: A mature male fish
options.c: A sexually mature female fish
options.d: A fish larva right after hatching

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-03.explanation: 'Rogner' refers to a sexually mature female fish carrying or releasing roe (fish eggs). The male counterpart, which releases milt (sperm), is called a 'Milchner'.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-04.question: Which fish group typically has pharyngeal (throat) teeth instead of jaw teeth?

options.a: Salmonids (e.g. trout)
options.b: Cyprinids (carp-family fish, e.g. bream, roach, carp)
options.c: Perch-family fish (e.g. zander, perch)
options.d: Cod-family fish (e.g. burbot)

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-04.explanation: Cyprinids (carp-family fish) lack true jaw teeth and instead have strong pharyngeal (throat) teeth that grind food against a hard pad in the throat. The shape of these teeth is also used to help identify species.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-05.question: Why are fish called 'poikilothermic' (cold-blooded) animals?

options.a: Because their body temperature adjusts to match the surrounding water temperature
options.b: Because they can regulate their own body temperature independently of the environment
options.c: Because their body temperature changes with age, regardless of water temperature
options.d: The term refers to coloration, not temperature

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-05.explanation: Fish are poikilothermic ('cold-blooded'): their body temperature largely tracks the surrounding water temperature, since unlike mammals and birds they do not maintain a constant internal body temperature. This strongly affects metabolism, activity level and spawning timing.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-06.question: Where does the European eel spawn, before its larvae drift back to Europe over several years?

options.a: In the Rhine, upstream of Cologne
options.b: In the Bay of Biscay
options.c: In the Sargasso Sea in the western Atlantic
options.d: In the North Sea off the Dutch coast

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-06.explanation: Sexually mature silver eels migrate thousands of kilometres to the Sargasso Sea in the western Atlantic to spawn. The hatched larvae (leptocephali) then drift back toward European coasts on the Gulf Stream over one to three years, transforming into glass eels along the way.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-07.question: Which fish species found in NRW has pelvic fins fused into a funnel-shaped adhesive disc that lets it cling to stones in fast-flowing water?

options.a: European perch
options.b: The bullhead (Groppe/Muehlkoppe)
options.c: The round goby (Marmorierte Grundel), an invasive goby species in the Rhine
options.d: Rudd

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-07.explanation: In gobies (Gobiidae), the pelvic fins are fused into a funnel-shaped adhesive disc (suction disc) that lets them cling to stones, for example in the fast-flowing Rhine. A well-known example in NRW is the introduced round goby (Marmorierte Grundel) in the Rhine. The bullhead (Groppe/Muehlkoppe), by contrast, has - like most fish - separate pelvic fins; it holds position using spread pectoral fins and camouflage on the riverbed.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-08.question: What is the function of the swim bladder in most fish?

options.a: It acts as a buoyancy organ that regulates swimming depth
options.b: It aids in digesting food
options.c: It excretes liquid waste products
options.d: It allows the fish to take up oxygen from the air

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-08.explanation: In most bony fish, the swim bladder is a gas-filled cavity that acts as a buoyancy organ: by regulating its gas content, the fish can hover nearly weightlessly at a given depth without constantly having to swim.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-09.question: What role do water fleas, cyclops and similar zooplankton play for a water body's fish population?

options.a: They have no discernible relevance to fish
options.b: Their main importance is producing oxygen in the water
options.c: They are an important food source, particularly for juvenile fish and plankton-feeding species
options.d: They are purely pests that endanger fish spawn

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-09.explanation: Zooplankton such as water fleas (Daphnia) and cyclopoid copepods form a key food source in a water body, especially for juvenile fish and plankton-feeding species like the vendace (Kleine Maraene). Abundant zooplankton is therefore an important indicator of good rearing conditions for young fish.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-10.question: What does a sub-terminal (underslung) mouth, as seen in barbel, nase and gudgeon, suggest about a fish's feeding behaviour?

options.a: The fish is a pure surface predator
options.b: The fish feeds predominantly on or near the bottom of the water body
options.c: The fish feeds exclusively on other fish
options.d: A sub-terminal mouth gives no information about feeding behaviour

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-10.explanation: A sub-terminal (underslung) mouth, found in barbel, nase and gudgeon, indicates bottom-oriented feeding: these species forage along the substrate for small invertebrates, algae and organic material. A superior (upward-pointing) mouth, by contrast, typically indicates surface feeding.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-11.question: What colour does the liver of a healthy freshwater fish typically have?

options.a: Whitish to yellowish, sometimes marbled
options.b: Distinctly bright red
options.c: Predominantly deep black
options.d: The liver is not visible in healthy fish

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-11.explanation: The liver of a healthy freshwater fish is typically whitish to yellowish, sometimes marbled in appearance. Markedly different colouring or changes in organs (e.g. the kidney) can indicate disease and should prompt caution before the fish is eaten.

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-12.question: Why are outmigrating juvenile salmon (smolts) in the Rhine catchment described as distinguishable from similarly-sized brown trout?

options.a: They cannot be distinguished at all; both species look identical at every stage
options.b: Only their weight differs; coloration is identical
options.c: Smolts show a characteristic silvery coloration and pectoral-fin features that set them apart from similarly-sized brown trout
options.d: The only difference is in the number of dorsal fin rays

angelschein-nrw-fischkunde-12.explanation: Before migrating to sea, juvenile salmon (smolts) undergo a physiological transformation (smoltification) that produces a distinctly silvery coloration; combined with pectoral-fin features, this lets them be told apart from similarly-sized brown trout - correctly recognizing them matters because salmon are protected year-round in NRW.

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-01.question: What must the person entitled to drain a body of water observe under §41 LFischG NRW?

options.a: They must first completely block the water off with traps
options.b: They must generally give the fishing-rights holder written notice of the start and expected duration of the draining at least one week in advance
options.c: No notice is required at all, as long as the draining happens outside the closed season
options.d: They only need to inform the lower water authority, not the fishing-rights holder

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-01.explanation: §41 LFischG NRW requires whoever is entitled to drain a body of water to give the fishing-rights holder written notice of the start and expected duration, generally at least one week in advance. Only in emergencies (e.g. flooding, ice, unforeseen repairs) may the fisheries authority allow draining before that period elapses; the person draining must then inform the fishing-rights holders without delay.

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-02.question: What is the first thing an angler should do on noticing a fish kill in an NRW water body?

options.a: Immediately notify the fire brigade/police and the regulatory office or lower water authority
options.b: First take water samples independently, only informing the authorities afterward
options.c: Wait and see whether the cause resolves itself
options.d: Only notify the water's owner by registered letter; the authorities are not responsible

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-02.explanation: On observing a fish kill, the fire brigade/police and the regulatory office or lower water authority should be notified immediately, so that cause investigation (e.g. water sampling upstream, downstream and near suspect discharges) and countermeasures can begin as quickly as possible. Delay significantly hampers evidence gathering.

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-03.question: May white water lilies and yellow water lilies be removed if they spread heavily in a water body?

options.a: Yes, they hinder angling and may be removed at any time
options.b: No, both species are legally protected and generally may not be removed
options.c: Yes, but only during the pike's closed season
options.d: Only the fishing leaseholder may decide on their removal, independent of nature conservation law

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-03.explanation: White water lilies and yellow water lilies are legally protected and generally may not be removed, even if they spread heavily and make angling harder - they provide important habitat and spawning substrate for fish and other aquatic life.

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-04.question: May an angler in NRW independently release non-native fish, e.g. from a garden pond or aquarium, into a body of water?

options.a: Yes, this increases biodiversity and is explicitly encouraged
options.b: Yes, as long as the animals appear healthy
options.c: No - releasing non-native species can be prohibited under the Landesfischereiverordnung, which is based on §42(1)(d) LFischG NRW, because it can endanger the water's appropriate fish population
options.d: Yes, but only into still waters with no inflow or outflow

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-04.explanation: §42(1)(d) LFischG NRW authorizes rules banning or restricting the release of fish species that could endanger a water's appropriate fish population. Non-native species from garden ponds or aquariums can outcompete native populations, introduce disease, or disrupt the ecological balance, and so may not be released without authorization.

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-05.question: Can activities other than angling also be restricted within a designated sanctuary zone (Schonbezirk)?

options.a: No, a sanctuary zone only ever concerns angling
options.b: Yes - §44(2) LFischG NRW allows mowing, removal of plants/silt/gravel, powerboating, water-skiing and ice sports within a sanctuary zone to be restricted or banned for set periods
options.c: No, sanctuary zones can only apply to commercial fishers, not recreational activities
options.d: Yes, but only hunting can additionally be restricted

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-05.explanation: §44(2) LFischG NRW allows a sanctuary zone to, for set periods, restrict or ban not just fishing but other activities that could disrupt reproduction or endanger the population - e.g. mowing, removing plants, silt, earth, sand, gravel and stones, powerboating, water-skiing and ice sports.

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-06.question: What is the purpose of fish passages (fish ladders) at weirs and dams under §45 LFischG NRW?

options.a: They let fish migrate past barrier structures; whoever built the structure must build and maintain the passage at their own cost
options.b: They serve purely as extra fishing spots for permit holders
options.c: They are purely decorative structures with no fisheries-biology function
options.d: They are used exclusively for power generation

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-06.explanation: §45(1) LFischG NRW requires whoever erects a barrier structure that significantly impairs fish movement to build and maintain a fish passage at their own expense. Fish passages let migratory species like salmon and eel get past weirs and dams; fishing within the passage itself is generally prohibited (§47(1) LFischG NRW).

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-07.question: Which authority is the 'upper fisheries authority' (obere Fischereibehoerde) in NRW?

options.a: The Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Agriculture and Consumer Protection
options.b: The county regulatory authority (Kreisordnungsbehoerde)
options.c: The district government (Bezirksregierung)
options.d: The relevant local angling club

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-07.explanation: Under §52 LFischG NRW, the Ministry is the supreme fisheries authority, the district government (Bezirksregierung) is the upper fisheries authority, and the county regulatory authority is the lower fisheries authority. The upper fisheries authority handles matters such as designating sanctuary zones (§44) and granting scientific-purpose exemptions (§39(2)).

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-08.question: Must an angler hand over their fishing documents on request to an officially appointed fisheries warden (Fischereiaufseher)?

options.a: Yes - under §31 Abs. 1 (i.V.m. §54) LFischG NRW the warden is authorized to check compliance with fisheries law, which includes requiring the documents to be shown
options.b: No, that is reserved exclusively for the police
options.c: Only if the fishing-rights holder is present at the same time
options.d: No, fisheries wardens may only observe, not carry out checks

angelschein-nrw-gewaesser-08.explanation: Officially appointed fisheries wardens are appointed under §54 LFischG NRW and are authorized, among other things, to inspect fishing gear, fish and fish containers. The duty to show the Fischereischein on request follows from §31(1) LFischG NRW (which names fisheries wardens as entitled to inspect it); the equivalent duty for the Erlaubnisschein follows from §37(1) LFischG NRW. Anglers must therefore hand over their documents on request.
